MP-0 (section 166.4).remaining: Sec. 6(1): the source's claim that I_{1:2}(G) < I_{1:2}(F) 'may be readily verified' cannot be checked against Lehmann's example, because Lehmann's distributions and the admissible range of alpha, c, p are not reproduced in KL 1951 and Lehmann 1950 is not held. Written: the masses (6.1) presupposes, both formulas, the difference, and the exact condition (holds for c < alpha; fails for p = 1/2, c >= alpha). Needed: E. L. Lehmann, 'Some principles of the theory of testing hypotheses', Annals of Mathematical Statistics 21 (1950), pp. 1-26, p. 2 (the example KL cite). The (2.7)-(2.9) hypotheses R1-R3 are this chapter's; the source's 'suitable assumptions' (Doob 1934, Trans. AMS 36, p. 774) are not held and are not attributed.

source_corrections: KL Theorem 4.1 (p. 83): 'equality iff T sufficient' fails when I(1:2) is infinite; stated with I(1:2) < infinity, with the counterexample thm:p15-w02b-p15-045-infinite-equality.
KL Theorem 4.2 (p. 84): same defect; stated under I(1:2) < infinity.

KL Sec. 6(2) (pp. 85-86): the printed J' for r = 2 is .0903; formula (6.2) gives .1806 (exactly twice), so the best grouping is r = 2 with efficiency .9095, not r = 1 with .6007 (a 40 percent loss). Recomputed in this session.

KL Sec. 6(1) (p. 85): I_{1:2}(G) < I_{1:2}(F) is not true for all parameter values of (6.1); it holds iff alpha(1-c) > 2c(1-alpha) sqrt(p(1-p)), in particular for c < alpha, and fails for p = 1/2, c >= alpha. Whether Lehmann's example restricts to the favourable range is unverified (Lehmann 1950 not held).
